:::{#exm-surprisal-chain-rule-noisy-copy}
#### Chain rule for surprisal with a noisy copy
<!-- no-figure: the example reports a handful of numbers, with nothing to plot -->

For the pair of values in @exm-joint-conditional-surprisal,
the [surprisal](#def-surprisal) of $x = 0$ plus the [conditional surprisal](#def-conditional-surprisal) of $y = 1$ given $x = 0$
is $`r round(s_x + s_y_given_x, 3)`$ [bits](#def-bit).
This sum is the [joint surprisal](#def-joint-surprisal) $\surprisalf{0, 1} = `r round(s_xy, 3)`$ bits <!-- check-term-links: allow -->
(@thm-surprisal-chain-rule).
Subtracting $\surprisalf{0} = `r round(s_x, 3)`$ bit from the joint surprisal <!-- check-term-links: allow -->
recovers $\surprisalf{1 \mid 0} = `r round(s_xy - s_x, 3)`$ bits
(@cor-conditional-surprisal-difference).

:::
